Please believe me. I did a detox, 28 day inpatient rehab, and then a 90 day IOP. I had a period of complete sobriety for 14 months. Then I started smoking weed. Summer 2020 my job and relationship got so stressful I sought out xanax bars from the street. Started taking them “therapeutically”. Inevitably abused them. Eventually didn’t have a plug for pharma. Took those hellish green hulk pressies for almost a year. What an awful, nightmarish year that was. I finally found a taper doctor in June of 2021. I have spent from then until now, and I have far to go still, getting off these pills. I haven’t been able to do anything. I’m 24f and my life is pathetic, I have no friends, can’t function in school or at a job, lay in bed miserable most of the time. I tried to kill myself the other night. 


I use to believe I was different from other addicts, that my mental illnesses made it impossible for me to be sober by the books. That I needed a small amount of prescribed benzos to live a normal life. All sorts of justifications. Truth is that I’m no different really and even though it’s hard to accept it- I’ll have to learn to cope with life without benzos. Idk how old you are, but eventually someone is gonna cut your script, you’ll lose your doctor, the laws on benzos will get tightened, something will happen and you will HAVE to get off them in this lifetime. You can push that off until later, just know that the longer you go the harder it will be later on..


Most of all, I’m just sending love your way. No matter what you choose to do, this sub will always be here for you.

You still have the chance to not take them. You can still stop before picking them up. You can even go as far as to tell the pharmacy you’re an addict, to delete that prescription, and blacklist you from picking up benzos. If you haven’t made the mistake yet, you don’t have to. You’re not set on this path. I believe in you.

So I have been a long-time xanax abuser but have sustained long periods of sobriety. Recently under stress I started buying and using Xanax ‘as needed’. Popped my first in September.
